record.paper_title: Open problems on structure of positively curved projective varieties
record.context_brief: Classification under positive holomorphic sectional curvature
record.original_question: Does the blow-up of a Hirzebruch surface admit positive holomorphic sectional curvature? More broadly, can all varieties of a fixed dimension, for example surfaces or threefolds, with semi-positive or positive holomorphic sectional curvature be classified, and can one identify an algebraic-geometric analogue of semi-positive or positive holomorphic sectional curvature?

evidence.quote: The complete classification is not known even in the case of surfaces.
It is not even obvious whether the blow-up of Hirzebruch surfaces has a positive holomorphic sectional curvature.
Does the blow-up of Hirzebruch surfaces admit a positive holomorphic sectional curvature?
Can we classify all the varieties of fixed dimension (e.g., dimension two or three) with semi-positive (or positive) holomorphic sectional curvature?
Can we find an analog of semi-positive (or positive) holomorphic sectional curvatures in algebraic geometry?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M, g)$ be a Kähler manifold with associated Kähler form $\omega$. The holomorphic sectional curvature of $g$ at a point $p \in M$ in the direction of a nonzero holomorphic tangent vector $v \in T_p^{1,0} M$ is defined by
$$H(v) = \frac{R(v, \bar v, v, \bar v)}{|v|^4},$$
where $R$ is the curvature tensor of $g$. The metric $g$ is said to have positive (resp. semi-positive) holomorphic sectional curvature if $H(v) > 0$ (resp. $H(v) \ge 0$) for every nonzero $v$.

For integers $n \ge 0$, the Hirzebruch surface $\Sigma_n$ is the projective bundle $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1} \oplus \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(n))$ over $\mathbb{P}^1$. Let $\widetilde{\Sigma}_n \to \Sigma_n$ be the blow-up of $\Sigma_n$ at one or more points.

(a) Does $\widetilde{\Sigma}_n$ admit a Kähler metric of positive holomorphic sectional curvature?

(b) Classify all smooth projective surfaces, and more generally smooth projective threefolds, that admit a Kähler metric of semi-positive (respectively positive) holomorphic sectional curvature.

(c) Identify an intrinsic algebraic-geometric property of a smooth projective variety that serves as an analogue of the existence of a Kähler metric of semi-positive (respectively positive) holomorphic sectional curvature.
artifact.status_search_result: Hitchin and later Yang–Zheng showed that every Hirzebruch surface/manifold admits Kähler metrics of positive holomorphic sectional curvature, but the question of whether arbitrary blow-ups of Hirzebruch surfaces admit such metrics, and the full classification of surfaces/threefolds with (semi-)positive holomorphic sectional curvature, are not resolved in the literature found. The problem is still posed as open in recent surveys.

status_evidence.title: Hirzebruch manifolds and positive holomorphic sectional curvature
status_evidence.snippet: Yang and Zheng proved that any Hirzebruch manifold admits a Kähler metric of positive holomorphic sectional curvature in each of its Kähler classes.
status_evidence.claim: Hirzebruch manifolds themselves are known to admit metrics with H>0, but the blow-up case is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Optimal pinching for the holomorphic sectional curvature of Hitchin's metrics on Hirzebruch surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Hodge metric on the n-th Hirzebruch surface with positive holomorphic sectional curvature with (1/(1+2n)^2)-pinching.
status_evidence.claim: Results focus on Hirzebruch surfaces themselves; no blow-up extension is established.

status_evidence.title: Examples of Complete Kähler Metrics with Nonnegative Holomorphic Sectional Curvature
status_evidence.snippet: Examples and classification questions for Kähler metrics with nonnegative holomorphic sectional curvature remain active.
status_evidence.claim: Classification in dimension 2 and 3 is an active open problem.
